purpose: Machine-readable evidence routing overlay for launch checks 19-36. This overlay does not create findings or PASS results.
no_pass_rule: PASS requires concrete evidence under the canonical SecHelix verification and release contracts.

checks.title: XSS
checks.evidence_required: Attacker-controlled content is reachable at a browser script-capable sink and can execute in the assessed context, or the code/config evidence establishes the same boundary failure.
checks.refuted_if: Context-correct encoding/text insertion, safe URL schemes and framework behavior prevent execution on every reachable sink.
checks.safe_test: Use only the deterministic SecHelix browser marker proof on LOCAL or authorized STAGING.

checks.title: CSRF
checks.evidence_required: A browser-authenticated state-changing route can be triggered cross-site without an effective anti-CSRF boundary.
checks.refuted_if: Relevant routes enforce a framework CSRF token and/or trustworthy Origin/Fetch-Metadata policy with cookie settings appropriate to the flow.
checks.safe_test: Use one bounded fixture state change; never operate on production accounts or money.

checks.title: Insecure file uploads
checks.evidence_required: An attacker-controlled upload can bypass size/type/content/name/storage/parser/serving controls and cross a security boundary.
checks.refuted_if: Uploads are size-bounded, content-validated, safely named/stored, parsed in a constrained boundary and served without unintended execution or cross-tenant access.
checks.safe_test: Use inert fixture files only; no polyglot malware, persistence or production storage mutation.

checks.title: Path traversal
checks.evidence_required: A caller-controlled path resolves outside the intended storage root after all decoding/canonicalization steps.
checks.refuted_if: The final resolved path is proven contained in the intended root and absolute/traversal/encoded traversal variants are rejected.
checks.safe_test: Use a temporary LOCAL fixture root and inert files.

checks.title: SSRF
checks.evidence_required: Attacker-controlled URL input can cause the server to contact a forbidden scheme/host/private address or can reach one through DNS/redirect changes.
checks.refuted_if: Every request hop enforces approved schemes and destinations immediately before connection, including redirects and resolved IP ranges.
checks.safe_test: Use only an allowlisted LOCAL callback under TargetScope.

checks.title: Broken password reset
checks.evidence_required: A reset/recovery token or flow can be guessed, replayed, reused after success/expiry, redirected to the wrong subject, or completed without required step-up.
checks.refuted_if: Tokens are high-entropy, short-lived, subject-bound, single-use, invalidated on completion, and recovery does not weaken required authentication boundaries.
checks.safe_test: Use seeded test identities and fixture mail/token delivery; do not send real email/SMS.

checks.title: Weak session management
checks.evidence_required: A session survives a boundary where it must rotate/revoke, remains valid after logout/revocation, or lacks required cookie/token lifecycle controls.
checks.refuted_if: Session identifiers rotate on privilege changes and are invalid after logout/revocation/expiry with appropriate cookie/token protections.
checks.safe_test: Use a fresh fixture session and explicit local/staging revocation hook.

checks.title: JWT secrets and validation
checks.evidence_required: A JWT is accepted when its signature/algorithm/issuer/audience/expiry/required claims are not valid under trusted configuration.
checks.refuted_if: Verification pins allowed algorithms and trusted keys plus issuer/audience/expiry and all required claims before authority is derived.
checks.safe_test: Use locally generated fixture tokens only; never capture or mutate real bearer tokens.

checks.title: Permissive CORS
checks.evidence_required: An attacker-controlled Origin receives credentialed or sensitive cross-origin access not required by the application.
checks.refuted_if: Allowed origins, methods, headers and credential behavior are explicit and untrusted origins cannot read protected responses.
checks.safe_test: Use OPTIONS/read-only requests with fixture identities; do not expose production secrets in the test.

checks.title: Rate limits
checks.evidence_required: An abuse-sensitive endpoint permits a bounded sequence of requests to exceed the documented per-subject/origin/action invariant before enforcement.
checks.refuted_if: Server-side counters/quotas/idempotency or equivalent controls stop the bounded abuse case without relying on client throttling.
checks.safe_test: Use a very small predeclared request budget; never load-test, brute-force or exhaust resources.

checks.title: Exposed environments
checks.evidence_required: A non-production environment is reachable with weaker controls while retaining production secrets, customer data, privileged tooling or trust connectivity.
checks.refuted_if: Staging/test has appropriate authentication and strict separation from production secrets/data/admin trust, with only explicitly required connectivity.
checks.safe_test: Prefer configuration and read-only checks; never pivot from staging into production.

checks.title: Default credentials
checks.evidence_required: A documented vendor/bootstrap/default credential or default account can authenticate to the assessed environment.
checks.refuted_if: Known default identities/tokens are disabled, removed or rotated before exposure, and bootstrap credentials cannot authenticate.
checks.safe_test: Test only explicitly documented defaults once against a fixture/staging target; no guessing or credential stuffing.

checks.title: Unsigned webhooks
checks.evidence_required: A webhook can cause a side effect without valid provider authenticity or can replay a previously valid event to create an extra effect.
checks.refuted_if: Signature/MAC verification happens before trust, freshness/replay/idempotency is enforced, and state readback proves exactly-once behavior.
checks.safe_test: Use the bounded webhook signature/replay fixture with local state readback.

checks.title: Frontend payment checks
checks.evidence_required: Client-controlled price/paid state/quantity/ownership/entitlement can alter trusted money or entitlement state, or repeated transitions violate an accounting invariant.
checks.refuted_if: Server/provider state is authoritative and payment/ledger/entitlement transitions preserve exact documented invariants across retries and concurrency.
checks.safe_test: Use mocks/fixtures/staging provider state; never place real purchases or mutate customer balances.

checks.title: IDOR / BOLA
checks.evidence_required: A subject can access another subject/tenant object by controlling or guessing an object identifier or alternate route.
checks.refuted_if: Every object/action lookup binds the authenticated subject/tenant/role at the trusted server/data-policy boundary.
checks.safe_test: Use two seeded identities and one fixture object under the bounded IDOR proof.

checks.title: APIs + user input authority
checks.evidence_required: Client-supplied role/owner/tenant/subject fields can become trusted authority or mass-assign privileged fields.
checks.refuted_if: Identity and privilege are derived only from trusted authentication/context and server allowlists ignore/reject authority-bearing request fields.
checks.safe_test: Use fixture requests with inert privilege-field changes; do not modify production identities.

checks.title: Exposed logs
checks.evidence_required: Passwords, tokens, payment secrets or unnecessary sensitive PII are persisted to application/CI/observability logs accessible beyond the minimum required audience.
checks.refuted_if: Sensitive values are redacted/minimized before persistence, access is restricted and retention matches the data class.
checks.safe_test: Use synthetic canary values; never inject real secrets just to test logging.

checks.title: Exposed source maps
checks.evidence_required: A deployed source map/debug/build artifact exposes unintended sensitive source, secrets, internal endpoints or other material that changes the attacker capability.
checks.refuted_if: Production artifacts either omit source maps/debug bundles or expose only material intentionally public and free of secrets/sensitive internals.
checks.safe_test: Use read-only artifact inspection; source-map presence alone is not a finding.
